verses.24:1: A vós, Senhor, {levavi} a minha alma: * meu Deus, em vós confio, {erubescam}.
verses.24:3: Nem riam de mim os meus inimigos: * pois todos os que {sustinent} não serão envergonhados.
verses.24:4b: Mostrai-me, Senhor, os vossos caminhos: * e {edoce} as vossas veredas.
verses.24:5: {dirige} na vossa verdade, e {doce}: * porque vós sois, Deus, {salvator}, e {sustinui} o dia todo.
verses.24:6: {reminiscere} das vossas compaixões, Senhor, * e das vossas misericórdias, que são desde sempre.
verses.24:7: Das {delicta} da minha juventude, * e das minhas {ignorantias} {memineris}.
verses.24:7b: Segundo a vossa misericórdia {memento}: * por causa da vossa bondade, Senhor.
verses.24:8: {dulcis} é o Senhor: * por isso {legem} aos que {delinquentibus} no caminho.
verses.24:9: {diriget} os {mansuetos} no juízo: * {docebit} aos {mites} os seus caminhos.
verses.24:10: Todos os caminhos do Senhor são misericórdia e verdade, * para os que {requirentibus} a sua {testamentum} e os seus testemunhos.
verses.24:11: Por causa do vosso nome, Senhor, {propitiaberis} ao meu pecado: * pois {multum}.
verses.24:12: Quem é o homem que teme o Senhor? * {statuit} uma lei no caminho que escolheu.
verses.24:13: A sua alma {demorabitur}: * e a sua descendência herdará a terra.
verses.24:14: O Senhor é o {firmamentum} dos que o temem: * e a sua {testamentum}, {manifestetur}.
verses.24:15: {oculi} para o Senhor: * porque ele {evellet} do laço os meus pés.
verses.24:16: {respice} para mim, e tende piedade de mim: * porque eu sou {unicus} e pobre.
verses.24:17: As tribulações do meu coração multiplicaram-se: * das minhas {necessitatibus} {erue}.
verses.24:18: Vede a minha humilhação e a minha fadiga: * e {dimitte} todas as minhas {delicta}.
verses.24:19: {respice} para os meus inimigos, porque se multiplicaram, * e com ódio iníquo me odiaram.
verses.24:20: Guardai a minha alma, e {erue}: * {erubescam}, porque esperei em vós.
verses.24:21: Os inocentes e os retos apegaram-se a mim: * porque {sustinui}.
verses.24:22: Livrai, Deus, Israel, * de todas as suas tribulações.

decisions.latin: Ad te, Dómine, levávi ánimam meam
decisions.why: leváre: 'lift up' (ἦρα). The line returns as a formula: 85:3 'quia ad te, Dómine, ánimam meam levávi', 142:8b 'quia ad te levávi ánimam meam' (grep), and the Introit and Offertory of the First Sunday of Advent open with it — DO's second Sunday after Epiphany responds 'Ad te, Dómine, levávi ánimam meam: * Deus meus, in te confído, non erubéscam' (Tempora/Epi2-0.txt, Responsory 7). levantar is leváre's in this psalter (118:48 'levávi manus meas'); elevar is eleváre's, erguer attóllere's (Ps 23). Douay-Rheims 'have I lifted up'; Matos Soares 1932 'elevei'.

options.label: levantei
options.note: Ruling: leváre's verb; the formula for 85:3 and 142:8b.

options.label: elevei
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: eleváre's verb in this psalter (8:2b; 23:7 'elevai-vos').

decisions.why: erubéscere → corar (glossary, open; D15 keeps it apart from confúndi → ser envergonhado, which comes in 24:3 and 24:4: the psalm sets the two side by side). The same two words close 24:1 and 24:20, one form in both. erubéscam may be future or present subjunctive; the Greek is an optative (μὴ καταισχυνθείην, 'may I not be put to shame'), Douay-Rheims reads 'let me not be ashamed' in 24:2 and 'I shall not be ashamed' in 24:20, Matos Soares 1932 'não seja eu envergonhado' both times. The future is kept: confidence ('em vós confio … não corarei'; 'esperei em vós … não corarei'), which the Latin allows and the Tuesday Prime antiphon 'Deus meus * in te confído non erubéscam' sings as a statement; the wish is option 2.

options.label: não corarei
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's verb, the future: confidence.

options.label: que eu não core
options.note: The Greek's optative (a wish); the Latin allows it.

options.label: não me envergonharei
options.note: The erubéscere row's option; merges with confúndi in 24:3.

decisions.why: sustinére with God as object: 'wait for, hold out for' (ὑπομένω). Three times in this psalm (24:3, 24:5, 24:21), always 'te'; 26:14 'Exspécta Dóminum … et sústine Dóminum' sets it beside exspectáre (→ aguardar, D24), and speráre in → esperar em comes in 24:20. So three verbs: esperar em (speráre), aguardar (exspectáre), 'esperar por' (sustinére) — the preposition keeps the last apart from speráre and says the waiting. Where sustinére is to endure a thing (68:8 'sustínui oppróbrium', 129:3 'quis sustinébit?') 'suportar' will serve; 15 lines in all (grep). Douay-Rheims 'wait on thee'; Matos Soares 1932 'esperam em ti' (merges with speráre).

options.label: esperam por vós
options.note: Ruling: waiting, apart from 'esperar em' (speráre, 24:20) by the preposition.

options.label: vos aguardam
options.note: exspectáre's verb (D24): merges two Latin verbs that stand side by side in 26:14.

options.label: esperam em vós
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: merges with speráre in (24:20).

decisions.latin: et te sustínui tota die … quia sustínui te
decisions.why: The same verb as 24:3 (decision sustinent), in the first person. In 24:5 the object comes first in the Latin ('te sustínui'); 'por vós esperei' keeps it there, and the same words close 24:21 ('quia sustínui te'), so the psalm's last line echoes 24:5 and ends on the verb. tota die → o dia todo (D24).

options.label: por vós esperei
options.note: Ruling: one wording for both places, 24:5's order.

options.label: esperei por vós
options.note: The plain order; 24:21's Latin order.

decisions.why: iníqua agere: 'doing wicked things' (ἀνομοῦντες, 'acting lawlessly'). The glossary keeps 'praticar a iniquidade' for operári iniquitátem (the Latin's frequent formula, 5:7a, 6:9); this is another build (neuter plural adjective with agere), so it takes the adverb. Douay-Rheims 'that act unjust things'; Matos Soares 1932 'que … cometem a iniquidade'.

options.label: agem iniquamente
options.note: Ruling: agere → agir; the adjective as an adverb, kept apart from operári iniquitátem.

options.label: fazem coisas iníquas
options.note: The neuter plural to the letter.

options.label: praticam a iniquidade
options.note: operári iniquitátem's formula — merges two builds.

decisions.why: supervácue: 'to no purpose, needlessly' (διὰ κενῆς). It stands alone after the mediant. Only here (grep). 'sem motivo' is gratis's word (34:7 has both 'gratis' and 'supervácue', grep: they must differ); 'em vão' (in vanum / in vano, 23:4) is the nearest. Douay-Rheims 'without cause'; Matos Soares 1932 'em vão'. The colon is short (2 syllables for 5).

options.label: em vão
options.note: Ruling: 'to no purpose' (Matos Soares 1932); shares 'em vão' with in vano (23:4).

options.label: sem proveito
options.note: Its own word, apart from in vano; the colon longer.

options.label: sem motivo
options.note: Douay-Rheims 'without cause': gratis's word (34:7 has both).

decisions.why: édocére ('teach thoroughly') and docére (24:5, 24:9) are one Greek verb (δίδαξον … δίδαξον … διδάξει): D15 lets them merge, and the psalm hears 'ensinar' three times. sémita → vereda (D15). demonstráre → mostrar (the Greek has γνώρισον, 'make known'; the Latin's verb is followed); 'Mostrai-me' is safe at the vós imperative (past 'mostrei'). The natural order (the verb first) is kept in both colons, the Latin puts the objects first.

options.label: ensinai-me
options.note: Ruling: one verb with docére (δίδαξον both).

options.label: instruí-me em
options.note: The ex- heard; erudíre's verb, and 'instruí-me' is a first-person past (rule 3).

decisions.why: docére → ensinar (glossary); 'ensinai-me' safe at the vós imperative.

options.label: ensinai-me
options.note: Ruling: glossary.

decisions.why: The glossary row 'dirígere at the vós imperative' (Ps 5:9) bans 'dirigi' ('I directed') and 'dirigi-me' ('I made my way to'), and leaves 'dírige me' (24:5, 26:11) to the psalm that meets it, naming 'encaminhai-me' as a candidate. Here the object is a person led into the truth (ὁδήγησόν με, 'guide me'): 'encaminhar' is to set someone on the way; safe (past 'encaminhei'). 24:9 díriget takes the same verb (decision diriget), so the psalm's one verb is heard twice. véritas → verdade (glossary).

options.label: Encaminhai-me
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's candidate; Matos Soares 1932's word in 24:9.

options.label: Guiai-me
options.note: The Greek's sense; 'guiar' is dedúcere's (22:3 'Guiou-me', 118:35).

options.label: Endireitai-me
options.note: The row's word for dírige with a road as object (5:9); with a person it is heard as 'straighten me up'.

decisions.why: The future of the verb of 24:5; the glossary lets the future be 'dirigir' (7:10 'dirigireis o justo'), but in one psalm one verb twice is heard as one: 'encaminhará', as 24:5. Matos Soares 1932 'Conduzirá'; Douay-Rheims 'He will guide'.

options.label: Encaminhará
options.note: Ruling: 24:5's verb.

options.label: Dirigirá
options.note: The glossary's future (7:10); the psalm's two places then differ.

decisions.latin: quia tu es, Deus, salvátor meus
decisions.why: salvátor: 'saviour' (ὁ σωτήρ μου). Ps 23:5 gave salutáris, in apposition to God and with the same Greek, 'Salvador' (decision salutari there); D15's test lets the two Latin words merge on one Greek word. 'Deus' stays a vocative between commas, as the Latin sets it.

options.label: o meu Salvador
options.note: Ruling: the title, capital as Ps 23:5.

decisions.why: Three Latin verbs of remembering in two verses — reminísci (24:6), memínisse (24:7), meménto (24:7b) — are one Greek verb (μνήσθητι … μὴ μνησθῇς … μνήσθητί μου): D15 lets them merge, and 'lembrar-se' three times lets the listener hear the psalm's play (remember your mercies; do not remember my sins; remember me). 'Lembrai-vos' is safe (the enclitic, past 'lembrei-vos' is not said). miseratiónes → compaixões, misericórdiæ → misericórdias (glossary, open: side by side here); a sǽculo → desde sempre (glossary).

options.label: Lembrai-vos
options.note: Ruling: one verb for the three (one Greek verb).

options.label: Recordai-vos
options.note: reminísci apart from memínisse; the play of the three is lost.

decisions.latin: Delícta juventútis meæ, et ignorántias meas ne memíneris
decisions.why: The Latin puts the objects first and the verb last; the Office of the Dead sings the half-verse as an antiphon with its asterisk after the first word, 'Delícta * juventútis meæ, et ignorántias meas ne memíneris, Dómine' (Commune/C9.txt), so the Portuguese must open on the faults too: 'Das faltas da minha juventude, e das minhas ignorâncias não vos lembreis'. 'lembrar-se de' puts a 'de' before each object, which Portuguese allows in front of the verb.

options.label: não vos lembreis
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's order, for the antiphon.

options.label: não vos recordeis
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's verb; breaks the one-verb run of 24:6–7.

decisions.why: delíctum → falta (glossary, open; the row names 24:7). Twice in this psalm, with delinquéntibus between (24:8), one family. Kept apart from peccátum → pecado (24:11).

options.label: faltas
options.note: Ruling: glossary.

options.label: delitos
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: the police report.

decisions.why: ignorántia: the Latin's (and Greek's, ἀγνοίας) word for sins of ignorance, beside the faults of youth; the plural kept. Only here in the psalter (grep 'ignoran'). Douay-Rheims 'my ignorances'; Matos Soares 1932 'as minhas ignorâncias'. The blind reader will say whether it is heard as sins.

options.label: ignorâncias
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's word (both Vulgate-family versions).

options.label: faltas por ignorância
options.note: The sense explained; merges with delícta.

decisions.why: The third verb of the run (decision reminiscere); 'tu' is emphatic and stands last in the Latin and the Greek (μνήσθητί μου σύ): 'you — not my sins — remember me'. Kept at the mediant as 'vós'. Douay-Rheims 'remember thou me'; Matos Soares 1932 drops it.

options.label: lembrai-vos de mim, vós
options.note: Ruling: the emphatic pronoun kept, where the Latin has it.

options.label: lembrai-vos de mim
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: 'tu' dropped.

options.label: vós, lembrai-vos de mim
options.note: The pronoun first, where Portuguese puts emphasis.

decisions.why: dulcis: 'sweet' (χρηστός, 'kind, good'). The Latin's word is kept (Douay-Rheims 'sweet'; Matos Soares 1932 'Doce'); dulcédo → doçura (glossary, 20:4) is the family. The copula is supplied (the Latin has none), after the pair, as the natural order. rectus → reto (glossary rectus corde).

options.label: Doce e reto
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's word.

options.label: Bom e reto
options.note: The Greek's sense; bonus's word.

decisions.why: legem dare: 'give a law' (νομοθετήσει, 'will legislate for'). lex → lei (D15). The indefinite 'uma lei' as 24:12 'legem státuit ei' ('firmou-lhe uma lei'). Douay-Rheims 'he will give a law to sinners'; Matos Soares 1932 explains ('mostrará aos pecadores o caminho que devem seguir').

options.label: dará uma lei
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's words.

options.label: dará lei
options.note: Without the article; 'dar lei' is heard as 'lay down the law'.

decisions.why: delínquere → cometer faltas (glossary, open; apart from peccáre → pecar, which Douay-Rheims and Matos Soares 1932 merge here as 'sinners'). The family of 24:7 and 24:18 'faltas'. in via → no caminho (via → caminho).

options.label: cometem faltas
options.note: Ruling: glossary.

options.label: pecam
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 'pecadores': peccáre's word.

decisions.why: mansuétus and mitis are one Greek word here (πραεῖς … πραεῖς): D15 lets them merge, and the Latin's parallel then sounds as the Greek's does, 'os mansos … aos mansos'. mitis is the Beatitude's word ('Beáti mites', 'Bem-aventurados os mansos'); mansuétus elsewhere 33:3, 36:11, 75:10, 146:6, 149:4 and mansuetúdo 44:5b, 89:10, 131:1 (grep, 9 lines) — the whole family can be 'manso / mansidão'. Douay-Rheims 'the mild … the meek'; Matos Soares 1932 'os dóceis … os humildes'.

options.label: mansos … mansos
options.note: Ruling: one Greek word, one Portuguese word; the Beatitude's.

options.label: brandos … mansos
options.note: Two Latin words kept apart (Douay-Rheims 'mild … meek').

decisions.why: docére → ensinar (glossary; 24:4b, 24:5). The Latin's two accusatives become 'ensinará aos mansos os seus caminhos'.

options.label: ensinará
options.note: Ruling: glossary.

decisions.why: requírere: 'seek, search for' (ἐκζητοῦσιν). quǽrere → buscar (glossary; 23:6 twice); requírere is another verb, and the glossary gives it 'pedir contas' only when God requires blood or sin (9:13, 9:34). Here the covenant is sought: 'procurar' keeps it apart from buscar. Douay-Rheims 'seek after'; Matos Soares 1932 'buscam'.

options.label: procuram
options.note: Ruling: a verb of its own, apart from quǽrere → buscar.

options.label: buscam
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: merges with quǽrere.

decisions.why: testaméntum is the Latin's word for the covenant (διαθήκη): 21 lines in the psalter (grep: 24:10, 24:14, 43:18, 49:5, 49:16, 54:21, 73:20, 77:10, 77:37, 82:6, 88:4, 88:29, 88:35, 88:40, 102:17, 104:8, 104:10, 105:45, 110:5b, 110:9a, 131:12a). 'testamento' is a will, or a Testament of the Bible, in Brazil: a wrong first hearing. 'aliança' is the Church's word and both Vulgate-family versions' (Douay-Rheims 'covenant'; Matos Soares 1932 'aliança'). testimónia → testemunhos (D15) beside it in 24:10 keeps the Latin's two words apart. It is feminine: 'a sua aliança' (the slot carries the article).

options.label: aliança
options.note: Ruling: the covenant, as heard today.

options.label: testamento
options.note: The cognate: heard as a will. (The possessive before it would need to be masculine.)

decisions.why: propitiári + dative: 'be propitious, be merciful to' (ἱλάσῃ τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ μου, 'make atonement for, be gracious about my sin'). Seven places with the family (grep: 24:11, 64:4, 77:38, 78:9 'propítius esto peccátis nostris', 98:8, 102:3 'Qui propitiátur ómnibus iniquitátibus tuis', 129:4a propitiátio). 'ser propício' keeps the Latin word; the risk is a first hearing 'favourable to my sin' — this draft tests it with the blind reader. 'perdoar' is plainer but is dimíttere's in 24:18 ('perdoai todas as minhas faltas'). Douay-Rheims 'thou wilt pardon'; Matos Soares 1932 'me hás-de perdoar'. multum est enim → 'pois é grande' (decision multum).

options.label: sereis propício
options.note: Ruling (to be tested): the Latin's word; 78:9 'sede propício aos nossos pecados' would follow.

options.label: perdoareis
options.note: Both Vulgate-family versions; merges with dimíttere (24:18).

options.label: sereis indulgente
options.note: Mercy to the sinner; weaker than the Latin.

decisions.why: multum est: 'it is much, great' (πολλὴ γάρ ἐστιν). 'é muito' is not said of a sin; 'é grande' is (Douay-Rheims 'for it is great'; Matos Soares 1932 'porque é grande').

options.label: é grande
options.note: Ruling: both Vulgate-family versions.

options.label: é muito
options.note: The Latin's word; not said of a sin.

decisions.latin: legem státuit ei in via, quam elégit
decisions.why: statúere → firmar (glossary, open; 118:38 'Firmai o vosso dito'). The subject is unnamed in the Latin (God, by the sense); the Greek has a future (νομοθετήσει), the Latin a perfect, which is kept. 'quam elégit' — the way the man chose (or God chose for him); 'que escolheu' keeps both. Douay-Rheims 'He hath appointed him a law'; Matos Soares 1932 '(Deus) fixou-lhe uma lei'.

options.label: firmou-lhe
options.note: Ruling: glossary.

options.label: estabeleceu-lhe
options.note: constitúere's verb in this psalter.

options.label: fixou-lhe
options.note: Matos Soares 1932.

decisions.why: demorári: 'linger, stay, abide' (αὐλισθήσεται, 'shall lodge'). Two places (grep: 24:13, 29:6 'Ad vésperum demorábitur fletus'): 'demorar-se' serves both (29:6 'à tarde se demorará o pranto'). in bonis → 'entre coisas boas' (the neuter plural; not 'goods' as property). Douay-Rheims 'shall dwell in good things'; Matos Soares 1932 'repousará entre bens'.

options.label: se demorará entre coisas boas
options.note: Ruling: the verb for both its places; the neuter plural as 'coisas boas'.

options.label: habitará entre bens
options.note: Douay-Rheims 'dwell'; habitáre's verb; 'bens' heard as property.

options.label: repousará entre bens
options.note: Matos Soares 1932.

decisions.why: D31: firmaméntum said of God → esteio (the row names this verse). The dative 'timéntibus' → 'dos que o temem'. The Greek adds a colon ('and the name of the Lord of those who fear him') that the Latin does not have — not reproduced.

options.label: esteio
options.note: Ruling: D31.

decisions.latin: et testaméntum ipsíus ut manifestétur illis
decisions.why: A purpose clause hanging on a noun without a verb (the Greek: 'and his covenant, to show them'); both Vulgate-family versions supply a finite verb ('his covenant shall be made manifest to them'; 'manifestar-lhes-á a sua aliança'). The Latin's shape is kept — 'e a sua aliança, para que lhes seja manifestada': the parallel with the first colon makes the sense (the Lord is their support, and his covenant is there to be shown them).

options.label: para que lhes seja manifestada
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's hanging clause kept.

options.label: lhes será manifestada
options.note: Douay-Rheims: a future supplied (the verse then reads 'e a sua aliança, lhes será manifestada' — would need the comma removed).

decisions.why: Verbless in Latin and Greek; the Matins antiphon sings it so ('Óculi mei * semper ad Dóminum', Psalmi matutinum.txt). A comma carries the missing verb. The glossary's respícere row (10:5b 'estão voltados para') gives the verb the draft would supply if the verbless line fails a reader.

options.label: Os meus olhos, sempre
options.note: Ruling: verbless, as the Latin and the antiphon.

options.label: Os meus olhos estão sempre voltados

forms.oculi: Os meus olhos estão sempre voltados

options.note: Matos Soares 1932's verb (and 10:5b's).

decisions.latin: quóniam ipse evéllet de láqueo pedes meos
decisions.why: evéllere: 'pluck out, tear out' (ἐκσπάσει). Three lines (grep: 24:15, 51:7 'evéllet te', 128:6 'priúsquam evellátur'). 'arrancar' is its first sense; it is also the glossary's erípere with a source (erípere is another Greek verb, ῥύομαι) — the two never stand in one verse, and in this psalm érue takes 'libertar' (decision erue). láqueus → laço (glossary). Douay-Rheims 'pluck my feet out of the snare'; Matos Soares 1932 'tirar do laço'.

options.label: arrancará
options.note: Ruling: evéllere's first sense.

options.label: tirará
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: its own word, but weak.

decisions.latin: Réspice in me … Réspice inimícos meos
decisions.why: réspice: the glossary's respícere row leaves the imperative to 118:132 'Áspice in me' → 'Olhai para mim' (ἐπίβλεψον both); 24:16 'Réspice in me, et miserére mei' is that verse's build and takes its words ('Olhai para mim, e tende piedade de mim', 118:132). 24:19 has the same verb (the Greek ἰδέ there): 'Olhai para os meus inimigos'. 'Olhai' is safe (past 'olhei').

options.label: Olhai
options.note: Ruling: 118:132's words.

options.label: Voltai-vos
options.note: The re- heard; convértere's verb (6:5).

decisions.latin: quia únicus et pauper sum ego
decisions.why: únicus: 'only, alone' (μονογενής). Ps 21:21 'únicam meam' (the same Greek) is being rendered 'a minha única' by Ps 21's draft; there it is a noun (my only one, my life), here an adjective of a man left alone. 'só' says it; 'único' would be heard as 'unique'. pauper → pobre (glossary). ego is kept as 'eu', moved before the verb (Portuguese's place for it).

options.label: só
options.note: Ruling: alone (Douay-Rheims 'alone'; Matos Soares 1932 'só').

options.label: único
options.note: The Latin's word; heard as 'unique'.

decisions.why: necéssitas: 'distress, straits' (ἀνάγκαι). Six lines (grep: 24:17, 30:8, and the refrain 106:6, 13, 19, 28 'et de necessitátibus eórum …'). 'necessidades' keeps the Latin's word; it may be heard as 'needs' (things lacking) rather than straits — to be tested. Douay-Rheims 'my necessities'; Matos Soares 1932 'as minhas aflições'.

options.label: necessidades
options.note: Ruling (to be tested): the Latin's word (Douay-Rheims).

options.label: angústias
options.note: The sense (straits); angústia is the noun of angustiáre (tribulátio's neighbour).

options.label: aflições
options.note: Matos Soares 1932.

decisions.why: érue me twice in this psalm (24:17 with a source, 24:20 without). Ps 21's draft takes 'arrancar' for éruere with a source (21:21), which is also erípere's; the glossary's erípere row says 'arrancar' fails with no source named and 'libertar' is the verb that never fails (6:5, 118:153). One psalm, one Latin phrase twice: 'libertai-me' in both, so that it is heard twice; safe (past 'libertei'). 'livrar' is liberáre's (24:22), which stays apart. Proposal for the glossary: éruere → arrancar with a source, libertar without — and where one psalm has both, libertar in both.

options.label: libertai-me
options.note: Ruling: one wording for the psalm's two places.

options.label: arrancai-me
options.note: Ps 21's word with a source; fails at 24:20 (no source).

options.label: livrai-me
options.note: Douay-Rheims and Matos Soares 1932: liberáre's word (24:22).

decisions.why: dimíttere with sins as object: 'forgive' (ἄφες). The glossary's dimíttere (let go) → deixar ir is the Nunc dimittis sense; with sins the Church's word is 'perdoar' (the Our Father's 'dimítte nobis débita nostra'). 'perdoai' is safe (past 'perdoei'). univérsa → todas (glossary univérsus).

options.label: perdoai
options.note: Ruling: dimíttere of sins.

options.label: remi
options.note: Remission; not current.

choices.24:1: Deus meus → 'meu Deus' (the vocative). confídere in → confiar em (glossary; the row names 24:1).
choices.24:3: irridére → rir de (glossary). confúndi → ser envergonhado (D15; the glossary row). étenim → pois.
choices.24:4b: demonstráre → mostrar. Natural order (the verb first) in both colons.
choices.24:6: miseratiónes → compaixões, misericórdiæ → misericórdias (glossary); a sǽculo → desde sempre (glossary).
choices.24:10: misericórdia et véritas → 'são misericórdia e verdade' (the copula supplied). testimónia → testemunhos (D15).
choices.24:18: humílitas → humilhação (glossary; the row names 24:18), labor → fadiga (glossary). 'Vede' as 118:153 (the twin build).
choices.24:19: odísse → odiar; ódium iníquum → ódio iníquo (not at a cadence).
choices.24:20: custodíre → guardar; speráre in → esperar em.
choices.24:21: innocens → inocente, rectus → reto; adhærére → apegar-se a (glossary).
choices.24:22: liberáre → livrar (glossary). Israël without article, as a vocative-like proper name.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm24.txt, 23 prayed verses. DO repeats the ids 24:4 and 24:7 (two verses each): keyed 24:4/24:4b, 24:7/24:7b as the shared latin.readVerses now gives them (the coordinator's fix; the draft was first written with a private wrapper and re-keyed by ps022/rename_ids.py). There is no 24:2: DO joins the Greek's 1–2 in 24:1. No titulus (D7). The Hebrew is alphabetic: nothing to reproduce. DO's uses checked by grep: Tuesday Prime antiphon 'Deus meus * in te confído non erubéscam' (Psalmi minor.txt); Matins antiphon 'Óculi mei * semper ad Dóminum' (Psalmi matutinum.txt); Office of the Dead antiphon 'Delícta * juventútis meæ, et ignorántias meas ne memíneris, Dómine' (Commune/C9.txt — the Latin order kept for it); Epiphany II Responsory 7 'Ad te, Dómine, levávi ánimam meam: * Deus meus, in te confído, non erubéscam' (Tempora/Epi2-0.txt).

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps024.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932; no Diurnal text). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Repeats found with ps005/grep_latin.py: supervácue (1), testaméntum (21), propitiári family (7), demorári (2), éruere (10), necéssitas (5), dírige me (24:5, 26:11), levávi ánimam meam (3). Latin readings kept against the Hebrew: 24:3 'esperam por vós' and 24:4 'agem iniquamente em vão' (not 'the faithless'), 24:7 'ignorâncias' (not 'transgressions'), 24:8 'dará uma lei' (not 'instructs'), 24:13 'se demorará', 24:14 'esteio' (not 'friendship/counsel'), 24:17 'multiplicaram-se' and 'necessidades'. Kept against the Greek: 24:14 without the Greek's extra colon. Deliberately tested with the readers: 24:11 'sereis propício ao meu pecado', 24:17 'necessidades', 24:7 'ignorâncias', 24:15 verbless.
